medium_value.description: Define a conservative YAML syntax subset for automatic guard replacement and make both parser paths enforce it. Specify handling of expression wrappers, trailing comments, quoted scalars, tabs, and whitespace inside string literals; do not collapse whitespace inside quoted expression values.

Specify how local git failures are classified without depending solely on English stderr fragments. Test missing objects, missing repositories, permission failures, and alternate locale settings separately.
Document the timeout and cancellation behavior inherited by the additional contents request, and add a test proving that a stalled request terminates through the existing fallback within that bound.

Expand job-block termination to cover valid job identifiers containing digits and explicitly refuse unsupported quoted keys, duplicate keys, anchors, or aliases. Add fixtures where these constructs follow or define simple-release.

Specify safe replacement mechanics: reject symlink targets, verify the original line immediately before replacement, write through a temporary file in the same directory, preserve permissions, and emit the fixed notice only after successful replacement. Define a warning and return-0 behavior for write failures.

Verify that the contents API result represents a regular file at the requested commit before accepting its text. Preserve the local reader's rejection of symlinks and other unsupported object types, extending FileContentResult if necessary.

Replace the independently optional reviewignoreBasePatterns and reviewignoreBaseSource fields with one optional discriminated resolved-result object. Require source none to carry an empty pattern list and make source mandatory whenever resolved patterns are supplied.

Specify cache lookup using Map.has so cached undefined failures suppress repeat API calls, and define whether in-flight promises must also be cached. Add a restarted-attempt test for a failed API resolution.

Restrict the PR-mode validation downgrade to values proven to originate from the PR head configuration. Preserve source provenance through configuration merging and specify behavior for invalid CLI and environment overrides.

Add composition tests where a valid, permissive head value conflicts with a restrictive trusted value, including mixed valid and invalid scope keys. Require trusted scope replacement to occur before any selection or content-fetch decisions.

Define bounded, single-line rendering for filenames, provider error details, and validation reasons in stderr warnings, escaping control characters and excluding raw response bodies. Add newline-containing filename and error-detail fixtures.

Define warning deduplication across restarted attempts and base changes. Use explicit run-level state for the once-per-run API notice and specify whether failed-file warnings are once per path, revision, or attempt.

In § 5.1 step 1, end the simple-release block at the first non-blank, non-comment line whose indentation is ≤ J, instead of the job-id regex /^<J>[A-Za-z_-]+:/. Also define how J is read (indentation of the first non-blank, non-comment line after /^jobs:/).

Parameterise the FR-5 WARN so it says 'the default governs' when no trusted source exists (DEC-1055) and 'the trusted value governs' otherwise; also state in § 5.6 whether a syntactically unparseable head `.loa.config.yaml` in PR mode remains a hard error.

Move into Phase 0: switching `paged-fetch.ts` to import `SelectionConfig` from `./types.js` and deleting the intersection casts, and adapting the two `truncateFiles` call sites (`truncation.ts:1461, 1613`) to the new `BaseRead` return shape.

Align § 1.3 with § 5.2: the diagram shows a 5-argument `resolveBaseReviewignore` (no cache) and routes 'else' to getFileContent, while § 5.2 has 6 arguments and routes only `unknown_commit` to the API with `other` → undefined.
Name the operator-facing document (mount-loa README / scaffold docs) where `LOA_SCAFFOLD_FIX_RELEASE_GUARD=1` and the legacy-guard check are described, and add it to the C-1 file list in § 1.4.

State in § 6 and § 9 that the `undefined` fall-through applies the checkout `.reviewignore`, which on a PR run is the head-controlled copy, with only a degrade flag; and decide whether PR mode should instead apply no patterns when the base copy is unresolvable.
Add fixtures for: no `simple-release` job at all (and yq returning `null`) → silent; two job-level `if:` lines inside simple-release (the 'two or more' clause) → silent, same verdict from yq and awk.
Hoist the base-pattern resolution in `truncateFiles` into one helper (`resolveBasePatterns(config)`) called from both read sites instead of editing `truncation.ts:1461` and `:1613` separately.

Add a § 7 C-2 case where `getFileContent` throws a non-`GitProviderError` (e.g. a TypeError from a malformed adapter response) and assert the run continues with `base_unavailable`, plus a case asserting the notice line is emitted once per base sha.

Replace the hard-coded candidate indentation /^<J+2>if:/ with the indentation of the first child line under the `simple-release:` key, read from the file; add a 4-space-indented workflow fixture (legacy and allowlist variants) to § 7 C-1.

Make the awk scan the single authoritative detection path and drop the yq path (and its version-matching, python-yq stub and dual-run tests); or, if yq is kept, state that the rewrite always uses the awk-located line number and re-verifies that line normalises to LEGACY immediately before writing.

Specify the normalisation rules in § 5.1 fully: whether a `${{ ... }}` wrapper is stripped before comparison, how a trailing `# comment` is treated, and which quote styles (none, single, double) are accepted; add one fixture per accepted form.

Specify the write mechanics of fix mode: build the replacement line as `<original indent>if: <ALLOWLIST>` preserving the original quoting style, write via awk `-v` (or printf to a temp file + mv) rather than `sed -i`, and on an unwritable target emit a WARN and return 0.

In § 7 C-1, run every fixture with the library sourced under `set -euo pipefail` (as the callers do), and change 'PATH scrubbed' to 'a PATH that contains coreutils/awk/sed/grep but no yq' (e.g. a shim directory).
Classify `unknown_commit` by exit status of `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` (or run the git subprocess with `LC_ALL=C`) instead of matching the strings 'Not a valid object name' / 'bad object'.

State the cache semantics in § 5.2 step 4: whether an `undefined` outcome (API failure) is cached for the run, and that presence is tested with `Map.has()` rather than `get() === undefined`. Recommend caching only resolved outcomes (`base`/`none`) so a restarted attempt can retry after a transient rate-limit; split the § 7 test into 'cached success → no second call' and 'failed read → retried once on restart'.

Replace the two coupled optional fields `reviewignoreBasePatterns` / `reviewignoreBaseSource` with one optional object `reviewignoreBase?: { patterns: string[]; source: "base" | "none" }`, and specify that `truncateFiles` tests `!== undefined` (an empty array with source `none` must be honoured).

Emit the 'read through the contents API' line as an INFO/notice (not `WARN:`) or only under verbose, and reconcile 'once per run' (§ 4) with per-base-sha re-resolution (§ 5.2 step 4) by stating 'once per base sha'.

blockers.concern: Every contents API 404 is treated as proof that .reviewignore is absent. A SHA obtained from pulls/N does not prove that the contents endpoint can access that repository and commit; authorization restrictions can also surface as 404.
blockers.why_matters: An inaccessible policy file is recorded as successfully absent, with no degradation. This can bypass repository exclusions and any controls that depend on accurate coverage provenance.
blockers.recommendation: Distinguish confirmed path absence from repository or commit inaccessibility using a trusted tree lookup or equivalent provider evidence. Treat ambiguous 404 responses as unavailable and degraded.

blockers.concern: PR-mode validation suppression occurs inside the general resolveConfig function, but the design does not establish that every caller subsequently invokes applyTrustedReviewScope before consuming the returned configuration.
blockers.why_matters: A caller that uses the partially resolved configuration directly can silently receive defaults after an invalid scope value. Environment-based PR detection makes that behavior possible outside the intended review execution path.
blockers.recommendation: Make trusted-scope composition mandatory before producing an executable configuration, using a separate intermediate type or a single public resolution entry point. Test all production callers and ensure none consumes the intermediate configuration.

blockers.concern: The fallback scanner ends a job only at a key matching [A-Za-z_-]+. Valid job IDs containing digits or quoted keys do not match that boundary, so the scan can include later jobs and select their if: line.
blockers.why_matters: With the fix flag enabled, a workflow where simple-release has no condition and a later job has the legacy condition can cause the wrong job to be rewritten.
blockers.recommendation: Terminate the scan at any sibling mapping key or dedent, and refuse ambiguous YAML. Add fixtures with numbered and quoted job IDs, including a simple-release job without an if: followed by another job carrying the legacy text.

blockers.concern: The indentation-based scanner does not establish whether a matching if: line is inside a YAML block scalar. A valid multiline job value can contain text at the assumed child indentation that looks like an if: key.
blockers.why_matters: The scanner can report a false legacy guard or rewrite scalar content. Extracting the real condition with yq does not automatically prove that the physical line chosen for sed is the same YAML node.
blockers.recommendation: Track scalar boundaries and YAML structure, or conservatively refuse layouts that cannot be mapped unambiguously to a physical key. Test scalar text resembling job conditions and require node-to-line agreement before editing.

blockers.concern: When the trusted base read fails, selection applies checkout .reviewignore patterns. In a PR checkout, those patterns can be controlled by the PR author. Marking coverage degraded does not itself prevent those patterns from excluding files.
blockers.why_matters: A failed base read can allow an untrusted PR change to suppress review of its own files. The documented fallback therefore does not establish the claimed fail-closed behavior.
blockers.recommendation: On trusted-base failure, apply no checkout-derived exclusions or stop the review. If degraded reviews remain permitted, explicitly prevent them from producing an authoritative successful review result.
